oil.summary: WTI surged 4.01% to $78.26/bbl today, driven by a confluence of supply-side shocks, even as the week-on-week picture remains -6.40% amid lingering demand concerns. Ukraine's long-range drone strike on one of Russia's largest refineries tightened refined-product availability, supporting heating oil (+3.52% to $3.93/gal). Three tankers damaged in the Gulf amid escalating US-Iran conflict added fresh risk premium to crude. Offsetting factors capped the rally: Russia's July production climbed above 9 million bpd, the US temporarily eased Russia oil sanctions to suppress the price surge, and Aramco deepened Asian crude discounts ahead of a potential Hormuz transit deal. RBOB gasoline bucked the trend sharply, collapsing 4.47% to $2.7118/gal. CME options price a 77% probability of an OPEC cut at the next meeting, reflecting persistent demand anxiety beneath the geopolitical noise.
drivers: Ukrainian drone strike on major Russian refinery tightened refined-product supply and supported crude and heating oil
Three tankers damaged in the Gulf as US-Iran conflict escalates, injecting fresh geopolitical risk premium
Partial offset from record-high Russian crude output above 9 million bpd and a temporary US easing of Russia oil sanctions

gas.summary: The US-European gas divergence widened sharply today. Henry Hub fell 2.16% to $2.63/MMBtu, extending a brutal one-month slide of 18.12%, consistent with ample domestic supply signals and limited immediate cold-weather demand. TTF, by contrast, surged 6.19% to €55.65/MWh, reflecting European supply anxiety: Belgium's July LNG imports reportedly consisted entirely of Russian cargoes after the Iran war collapsed alternative flows, highlighting the continent's precarious position. Southeast Asia's gas shortages are diverting flexible LNG cargoes away from European spot markets, adding further upward pressure on TTF. Mexico's new fracking ban in a key shale basin removes a potential future supply source for North American and export markets. News flow for Henry Hub-specific catalysts is thin today beyond the broader supply-demand backdrop.
drivers: TTF jumped 6.19% as European LNG supply chains remain severely disrupted, with Belgian July receipts entirely from Russia following the Iran war
Southeast Asian gas shortages tightening global LNG availability and reducing cargo flexibility for European buyers
Henry Hub continued its month-long decline (-18.12%), reflecting domestic US supply resilience absent near-term demand catalysts

power.summary: EU carbon EUAs held near flat at $77.02/EUA (-0.12%), broadly stable on the week and month, masking significant stress in European power markets. Electricity prices in Europe spiked to €500/MWh as an intense summer drought curtailed hydropower and simultaneously drove air-conditioning demand sharply higher. The surging TTF (+6.19% today) raises gas-fired generation costs, compounding the squeeze. A drone attack on a UAE nuclear power plant earlier this week added a new dimension of infrastructure risk to the region. Longer-term structural signals remain constructive for clean energy: China added more nuclear capacity over the past decade than the rest of the world combined, and CNOOC launched the world's first 16MW floating wind turbine. Southeast Asia's gas-fired power buildout is stalling on supply and price pressures, underscoring the difficulty of transitioning away from coal.
drivers: European power prices spiked to €500/MWh on drought-driven hydro shortfalls and surging cooling demand, amplified by higher TTF gas costs
Drone attack on UAE nuclear power plant and ongoing Gulf conflict heighten regional energy infrastructure risk
China's record nuclear buildout and CNOOC's 16MW floating wind turbine debut highlight accelerating clean capacity growth outside Europe
